# Positional tabs: native reference

Original controls generated by `tools/positional_tabs_fixture.py`, without an
external document engine. `source.docx` passes eight schema checks. The reference application exported the 60-page `native.pdf`; `tools/positional_tabs_reference.py`
extracts the colored 4pt image markers and records source/PDF SHA-256 hashes.
Coordinates in `reference.json` use points and a top-left page origin.

The engine's positional-tab importer, field alignment, line breaking and
serializer use these controls. Template 109's active footer needs this feature.

## Specification and observed divergence

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.23 says positional tabs ignore custom/default tabs,
align following text relative to margins or indents, and move to the next
available line when the target has been passed. Its margin-relative example
explicitly ignores paragraph indents. Attribute types are §17.18.71–73.

These controls have 72pt page margins on a 612pt-wide page, custom ordinary
tab stops at 72 and 108pt, and independently varied paragraph indents.
Native observations (short aligned fields, no collisions):

- Margin-center anchors at 306pt regardless of left/right/first-line indents.
- Indent-center anchors at `306 + leftIndent / 2`. A 36pt left indent gives
  324pt, while a -18pt left indent gives 297pt. Right and first-line indents
  do not change this anchor. In particular, a 24pt right indent does **not**
  reduce the anchor by 12pt as centering between both indents would suggest.
- Both right-alignment modes anchor at `540 - rightIndent`. Margin-relative
  right alignment therefore does not ignore the paragraph right indent.
- A leading left positional tab stays at the current indented first-line
  start, including hanging indentation, instead of adding an empty line or
  moving backwards to the margin. After preceding text it moves to a new
  line. With a positive left indent, both modes start that line at the indent;
  with -18pt left indentation, margin mode starts at 72pt and indent mode at
  54pt. This contradicts simply resetting margin-left tabs to the margin in
  all cases.
- The long-prefix center case wraps the aligned field onto the next line.
- Dot, hyphen, underscore and middle-dot leaders fill the gap before the
  aligned field, without shifting its center.

Image-derived field anchors avoid relying on identical Arial glyph widths
between the reference application and the browser. The PDF and source remain the evidence if an
inferred rule needs refinement.

`contexts.docx` and `contexts-autofit.docx` add three pages each with header,
footer, two-column, fixed-table and AutoFit-table controls, plus repeated
positional tabs. Generate both with `tools/positional_tabs_context_fixture.py`;
the context reference extractor accepts the basename as its optional argument.
The contextual native captures confirm that columns/cells use their local
writing area and that page stories use the page margins. Before a subsequent
tab, the reference application excludes trailing spaces from the preceding positional field's
alignment, while retaining their advance. The browser checks these field
anchors and line breaks against the native reference captures.

Unit coverage includes all 60 body controls, required-attribute validation,
typing after/replacing a positional tab, run formatting, exact undo,
discretionary measurement and export/reopen. Browser coverage checks native
geometry and editing with untouched-package preservation. These controls do
not certify every combination of oversized aligned text and floating wraps.

Reproduce: generate the source with Python, open that exact file in the
reference application and export it as PDF, then run the reference extractor. Do not regenerate
the source without also replacing its native PDF and reference hashes.
